review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped for uses of `round` in the ConwayRefinement sources. The simp surface is small. `round_zero` and `round_neg` are tagged `@[simp]` and point in sensible normal-form directions: `round_zero` has a closed RHS, and `round_neg` pushes negation outward. I saw no sign of a loop or of competing rules between them. `round_of_pos` unfolds `round` into a dependent-proof `ofSets` cut. `round_mk_of_pos` has an instance-carrying `@mk` right-hand side. Neither is suitable as a simp lemma, so leaving them unannotated is justified. `round_of_nonpos` is conditional and could be simp, but its three uses (lines 198, 205, 214) are single `rw` or `simp_rw` calls right after a `le_or_gt` case split. The other uses of `round` that I found are in `OmnificInteger/Basic.lean`, `OmnificInteger/NormalForm.lean` and `HahnSeries/NormalFormAdd.lean`. Those rewrite with `round_of_pos` or state `round` equalities as hypotheses, not through simp. I found no practical benefit that would justify the annotation. I did not check the `!{...}` notation or the `Surreal` simp set for overlap with `round_neg`. I did not run Lean, so nothing here depends on how the simplifier behaves.
